About.title: Sobre mí
About.badge: Estudiante de Ingeniería de Software con experiencia práctica en tecnología
About.p1: Soy estudiante de Ingeniería de Software y actualmente trabajo en el área administrativa, donde también doy soporte a sistemas, equipos y mejoras de procesos con tecnología.
About.p2: Hoy concentro mis estudios en back-end, APIs, Java y Spring Boot, sin dejar de usar React, TypeScript y Python cuando el problema necesita una solución más completa.
About.quote: Me gusta entender primero el problema y usar tecnología para simplificar lo que antes daba trabajo.

AboutModern.p1: Mi formación en Ingeniería de Software va acompañada de proyectos en los que tuve que pensar en arquitectura, persistencia, autenticación, APIs, pruebas y experiencia de uso — no solo en construir pantallas.
AboutModern.p2: También llevo a mis proyectos lo que aprendo trabajando con procesos administrativos y soporte de TI: observar el flujo real, identificar fricciones y automatizar lo que tiene sentido.
AboutModern.bullet1: Java, Spring Boot y APIs REST
AboutModern.philosophy_text: Entender bien el problema, construir algo mantenible y comprobar que funciona.

common.source_note: The claims on this page point to public documentation and code.

leve.meta_description: Leve engineering decisions: command API, explicit revisions, conflicts and offline support.
leve.title: Leve
leve.summary: A personal planner built to preserve changes when the network fails, a request is repeated or two sessions edit the same data.
leve.problem_body: Planner applications can hide synchronization failures and overwrite concurrent changes. Leve treats preserving user data as its main constraint and makes pending states and conflicts visible.

commandApi.title: One write path
commandApi.body: Every mutation goes through POST /api/commands. The API centralizes validation, authorization, operationId idempotency and operation records.

revision.title: Expected revisions instead of last-write-wins
revision.body: Every command declares the revision it expects. When the server finds another version, it rejects the write and returns the concurrent state so the interface can preserve the conflict.

offline.title: Explicit, reversible offline mode
offline.body: Offline mode is opt-in. Changes made without a connection enter a local outbox and synchronize after reconnection; the interface reports what is still pending.

domain.title: Shared rules
domain.body: Client and server import the same Zod schemas from the domain package, reducing divergent validation between the two layers.

commandShape.title: Consistency through a less conventional API
commandShape.body: The single endpoint simplifies cross-cutting guarantees, but replaces REST routes per resource with commands discriminated in the payload.

localData.title: Continuity requires local data
localData.body: The outbox preserves work without a network, but the cache can retain personal data on the device. Activation therefore depends on an informed user choice.

freeTier.title: Architecture shaped by the free tier
freeTier.body: The project documents paginated cleanup, scheduler leases and controlled Firestore reads as choices required to operate without paid resources.

leve.next_body: I would turn the checks that the README still marks as manual into a recorded release routine: push with the app closed, an external screen reader and installation on a physical device.

evidence.tests: The repository documents unit tests, emulator integration and Playwright E2E for two tabs, outbox reconnection, conflicts and accessibility.
evidence.privacy: Accounts can export versioned JSON, delete their data and control offline storage per device.
evidence.operation: The README records CI, runbooks and a matrix separating automated coverage from manual checks.

omni.meta_description: Omni architecture: Java, Spring Boot, PostgreSQL, multi-tenancy, bots and distributed operations.
omni.title: Omni
omni.summary: A clinic management and automation system that brings patients, appointments, confirmations and multiple clinic operations together.
omni.problem_body: Omni centralizes patients and appointments and automates confirmations while keeping different clinics' data separate. The solution combines a web dashboard, a domain API and automation bots.

layers.title: Layers with distinct responsibilities
layers.body: The API uses Java 17 and Spring Boot 3, the dashboard uses React and TypeScript, and automations run in Python. PostgreSQL stores transactional data.

tenant.title: Multi-tenancy through tenant_id
tenant.body: Isolation uses a tenant_id discriminator and Hibernate filters in the data access layer. Authentication uses JWT with automatic client-side refresh.

deployment.title: Distributed services
deployment.body: The frontend is deployed on Vercel, the backend runs in a container on Render, and PostgreSQL runs on Supabase with a managed connection pool.

observability.title: Per-request traceability
observability.body: The backend documents logs with requestId, userId and tenantId, plus a /health endpoint for the API and database connection.

isolation.title: Isolation concentrated in application code
isolation.body: The documentation states that the database does not use RLS: separation between clinics depends on tenant_id and filters applied in Java code.

coldStart.title: Free tier and cold starts
coldStart.body: The free Render service sleeps after inactivity. The frontend must explain that the API is waking up and offer a retry.

operations.title: More services, more operations
operations.body: Separating frontend, API, database and bots allows each layer to use a suitable tool, but expands secret configuration, monitoring and recovery procedures.

omni.next_body: I would follow the production guide's own recommendation and move the bots to a dedicated background worker. I would also add a second isolation boundary at the database layer to complement the application's tenant filters.

evidence.health: The monitoring guide describes /health with API and PostgreSQL connection status.
evidence.security: The documentation lists rate limiting on authentication routes and security headers configured in Spring.
evidence.database: Production uses PostgreSQL on Supabase through a connection pool; Docker Compose reproduces the database locally.
